en: What do you mean, a lesson?
A lesson? Oh, dear, you should talk to Mila, dear Mila, she's the teacher now. How time flies! Mine are administrative tasks, those are better for me...
No more lessons from me, no... The history of Rhos... I've always been in charge of administration. The Rada wouldn't exist if not for me! I got them off the ground, you know.
You mentioned a story?
Well, if you insist. I can tell you a story, yes.
Maybe some other time.
Oh, shame. The young, so snappy, so impatient!
Sure, why not.
Let me see... Let me see, then...
You said something about a task.
Well, we all have many tasks, dear. I have administrative duties, that's what I'm good at! Not that I like to brag.
I've always been in charge of administration. The Rada wouldn't have gotten off the ground without me, you know.
You used to teach Rhosian history?
Used to? I still do, only it's after-hours now, class is dismissed for today, I have many other tasks to see to...
Tell me some more about Rhos.
Certainly, let me get my materials ready... Oh, dear...
About stories, again...
Oh, you want to hear one? I have one I can tell...
(She has a condition...) Is someone looking after you?
What! Why would I need to be taken care of, my dear? I'm fine on my own.
I've got to leave.
Oh, I'm sorry, dear. Too tired for stories, now...
What do you know about this continent?

Oh, you want to talk Rhos! I've taught classes on this. Not just on the founding of cities and our greatest bogatyrs, but on the mythos of the land that holds us. The convergent and divergent tectonic dances that shaped not just the land but our souls, the pentimento of Mother Earth herself, Mat Zemlya, her etchings beneath this canvas of mud and moss!
It is beautiful, and although the Mist swallowed everything, still the mountains of Rhos are spread in front of us, still its earth pulses with something grander than the West will ever know.

My scientific mind wouldn't dream of defying the obvious sentience of our surroundings, dear student. Rhos is not just a place, but a living, breathing thing... The beating heart of the entire world, the center of all that is, the perfect and ultimate antithesis to the West. And so – the War.
Did you see the world before the War?
What can you tell me about Zalesye?

Important place before the terror bombings! The War destroyed our factories, my dear, and you see – we were important to this region, crucial even. A hub of commerce, bridging the gap between the vast Dola with its scattered villages and nomadic peoples – and the busy RO-29, the golden path towards the developed East!

In addition to that, a bustling industrial center, with many workers – pendular migrants – producing the stuff of riches day after day... Before the War co-opted all our production, with its relentless internal demand for steel...

Yes, we were important. Big. What remained of Svarog Factories is but a tiny fraction of what once was. And the city built right behind it, across from Lake Pavlie, sings to us its steel-willed memories... You can still hear the clinking and clanking, the sound of cargo trains, to and fro, to and fro...
Talking about something else...
I need to go, now.
Have I seen the world? I am the daughter of farmers! Farm work, farm work, farm work. I handled administrative tasks. They are my specialty.

Before the War? Well, the War was a most terrible thing. In War or in peace, one must tend to the crops, take care of supplies, oversee personnel. It's an important factor... I am good at administrative tasks, you see.

How rude! My eyesight's still good, you know. I can see you and your scrawny little face behind that mask. You must be one of the newer students... Today, we will learn of <u>supply lines</u> in the War and how we can learn from them...
I've gotten the Rada off the ground, you know. They would be nothing without me!
Oh, dear, curse my failing memory. There was a story about the War, the advent of Mist, that I wanted to tell... Used to teach it all the time.

"In the darkest days of the War, as mining equipment tore through uranium ore and nuclear reactors bombarded its isotopes, a merciless side-product would infest the air of an unassuming village in the West, undetected. The Mist.

Many years later, somehow this curse on Western hubris made its way into Rhosian reactors, and the Continent scrambled to understand why; every hypothesis led to contradictory conclusions on the conditions of its growth."
(Nod.)
I'll hear the rest later. (Leave)
What? Don't interrupt the lesson!

"And so the Mist spread through Rhos, and its destructive power greatly outran our meek countermeasures. All conflicts were hopelessly overturned in the West's favor, and their imperialist embargoes hit the Continent from every side. Panic was at a rise, and all was lost. Although an unconditional surrender to those Western pigs was bitterly agreed to, still there was no way to stop the Mist’s horror. Not that they cared...

The War came to an end as all living things in the Continent started to corrode and spread the Mist even further. Food and water were ruined, killing billions from lack of sustenance. What few technocrats and oligarchs remained were slaughtered by the oppressed over control of their farms and factories; justified uprisings against high-ranking degenerates. And of course, the fauna and flora were horribly mutated, as if led through a million years of evolution in the span of mere weeks."
I see.
About something more important...
I'll hear the rest later. (Leave)
Too smart for our class, I see?

"The abandoned nuclear reactors where the seeds of Mist were nurtured became known as the Thresholds, and few dared venture there. The superstructure of Continental society collapsed, scattering its people into primitive, isolationist villages – like present-day Zalesye.

In this new social configuration, a few scientists set up shop at the fringes of the Thresholds – so as to become specialized traders with the small populations that resided there. Today, we call them Mechanists. They became the chief accumulators of material and intellectual wealth in the new society that formed – a dynamic we're still struggling to uproot."
This new dynamic... Persists?
Let's talk about something else.
I'll hear the rest later. (Leave)
Oh, dear... Now I've lost my train of thought...
This stubborn tethering to pre-Mist divisions of labor... Yes, let's talk about those...
No, wait. I'm sorry... Seem to have lost my train of thought... Oh, my apologies, dear. I feel like I need a rest...
How do you get food?
Three meals a day, as is the norm! And if you're not Rada, you can still get meals from us! Just talk to Dmitri or Erlich, or maybe Pietra, she's always prancing about looking for something to do...
But I suppose there have been times when, for some reason, it's a damned Acolyte bringing my meals... Why? Is someone playing a prank on me?... You know I can't stand religious types!...
Is there someone you trust around here?
Why, I trust you, my dear. You're a trusted member of the Rada, after all! Always going on and on about how we should have more meetings, and teach Erlich to write proper minutes...

But yes, I suppose some of those religious fanatics from the Church will do me a favor if I need one. But I don't like them, no... They try to monopolize charity work, and always tie it to religion! The Rada is better for Zalesye, that much is obvious...
So... You are one of the founders of the Rada?
If it wasn't for me, there'd be no Rada! Boneheads with a heart of gold, is what I always say about them... Couldn't organize a rally even in pre-War times, if you ask me...
But still – I just had to help them. Hearts in the right place, and the theory, the theory is sound – they're very studious. And they wouldn't have recruited a single member without me!
Why don't we talk about something else.
I need to get going, I'm afraid.

Hi, dear. Sit down for your lesson.
Hello! Are you here for a meeting?
Yes, yes, I'm going... Be there at 5.
Can we talk?
I'd like to chat.
Wanna ask some things.
Going so soon, dear?
Yes, yes, bye now, dear.
Off you go, then! We'll meet on Thursday, as planned...

How could the Mist be anything but a Western evil, inflicted with no regard for non-combatants, just to win an unjust War? Somehow their spies planted it on all Rhosian reactors, mines, deposits – and of course, in the schools and hospitals... And by then we were helpless.

Why are you giving these to me, dear? Oh, I suppose you'll need recompense.
What is...? Oh, yes, this is what I was looking for. Thank you dear, next time I'll... Next time, I'll...
Huh? Why would I ever need a Vulture?
Hmm, I don't think I asked for anything. Why, what do you have? Or, wait... No, no, come back some other time.
I'll bring all of this to you.
You will? Why? Are you the delivery man?
I'll think about it.
Oh, I do nothing but think, day in and day out.
Got anything else?
You need someone to care for you...
I'm just glad you remembered to pay.
